classification.difficultyReason: The same task as p27-q11: compute two annuity balances with the geometric-series formula and compare them.

content.prompt: Compare the balances at the end of the investment periods in each part. Give monetary answers to the nearest cent.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Mia can invest $\$800$ at the end of each year for 20 years, or $\$1500$ at the end of each year for 10 years, in a fund that pays 6% p.a. Which is the better investment for Mia, and by how much?

answer.short: Investing $\$800$ annually for 20 years gives $\$29\,428.47$, compared with $\$19\,771.19$ for $\$1500$ annually for 10 years: $\$9657.28$ more.
answer.worked:
Option 1: $\$800$ at the end of each year for 20 years.

End of 20th year: $800(1.06)^{19}+800(1.06)^{18}+\cdots+800$

This is a geometric series with $a=800$, common ratio $R=1.06$ and $n=20$.

$$\begin{align*}FV_1&=\frac{800(1.06^{20}-1)}{1.06-1}\\&\approx\$29\,428.47\end{align*}$$

Option 2: $\$1500$ at the end of each year for 10 years.

End of 10th year: $1500(1.06)^{9}+1500(1.06)^{8}+\cdots+1500$

This is a geometric series with $a=1500$, common ratio $R=1.06$ and $n=10$.

$$\begin{align*}FV_2&=\frac{1500(1.06^{10}-1)}{1.06-1}\\&\approx\$19\,771.19\end{align*}$$

Using the unrounded balances,
$$FV_1-FV_2\approx\$9657.28$$

Therefore, investing $\$800$ annually for 20 years is better, by $\$9657.28$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Ruby invests $\$3000$ at the end of each year for 12 years. Fund A pays 4% p.a. and Fund B pays 6% p.a. Which fund gives Ruby the greater balance, and by how much?

answer.short: Fund B gives $\$50\,609.82$, compared with $\$45\,077.42$ for Fund A: $\$5532.41$ more.
answer.worked:
Fund A: $3000(1.04)^{11}+3000(1.04)^{10}+\cdots+3000$

This is a geometric series with $a=3000$, common ratio $R=1.04$ and $n=12$.

$$\begin{align*}FV_A&=\frac{3000(1.04^{12}-1)}{1.04-1}\\&\approx\$45\,077.42\end{align*}$$

Fund B: $3000(1.06)^{11}+3000(1.06)^{10}+\cdots+3000$

This is a geometric series with $a=3000$, common ratio $R=1.06$ and $n=12$.

$$\begin{align*}FV_B&=\frac{3000(1.06^{12}-1)}{1.06-1}\\&\approx\$50\,609.82\end{align*}$$

Using the unrounded balances,
$$FV_B-FV_A\approx\$5532.41$$

Therefore, Fund B gives the greater balance, by $\$5532.41$.
